text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today and is down 7.3% over two weeks, tracking a broader pullback in oil prices and shifting geopolitical risk. U.S. crude has weakened to $96.41 per barrel, and the immediate trigger appears to be cautious sentiment around U.S.-Iran negotiations — despite escalatory rhetoric from Trump this week, the fact that both sides are still talking at the U.N. has reduced the near-term risk premium that had been supporting oil prices.

The two-week decline also reflects the wider oil market's uncertainty: while prices remain elevated globally ($114.89 for world crude), the U.S. benchmark has fallen nearly 8% in the past week as diplomatic signals have temporarily outweighed war concerns. For an integrated oil company like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly compress margins and reduce the value of reserves in the ground, which is why the stock has tracked the oil weakness despite the company's strong operational position.
